verdict: T. Rowe Price grew revenue 6% to $2.0B on higher markets, but investment gains shrank and clients pulled $28.3B, leaving profit for shareholders down 5% at $612.3M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $2.87 a year ago; adjusted diluted EPS was $2.86

kpis.label: Assets under management
kpis.note: At Sep 30, 2026, +5.4% YoY; average AUM was $1,887.2B

kpis.label: Net client flows
kpis.note: Net outflows in the quarter, mostly from equity funds

segments.name: Investment advisory fees
segments.note: Fees for managing client money — equity $1,047.4M, multi-asset $537.6M, fixed income $118.7M and alternatives $92.7M. The average fee rate slipped to 37.8 basis points (0.378% a year).

segments.name: Capital allocation-based income
segments.note: Mostly the rise in accrued carried interest — the firm's share of profits in some funds — of $63.1M, less $3.2M of acquisition-related amortization and impairments.

segments.name: Administrative & other fees
segments.note: Administrative, distribution, servicing and other fees, including retirement-plan recordkeeping.

segments.name: Performance-based advisory fees
segments.note: Extra fees earned when funds beat their targets, mostly in alternatives strategies.

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for investment staff and everyone else — the firm's biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology & occupancy
opex.note: Technology, offices and facilities, including outsourced technology services.

opex.name: Distribution & servicing
opex.note: Paying distributors and servicing client accounts.

opex.name: G&A & other
opex.note: General, administrative and other running costs.

opex.name: Capital allocation compensation
opex.note: The share of carried-interest income passed on to employees as pay.

opex.name: Advertising & promotion
opex.note: Advertising and promoting the firm's funds and services.

opex.name: Acquisition amortization & other
opex.note: Acquisition-related amortization, impairments and other costs.

opex.name: Retention arrangements
opex.note: Pay tied to keeping staff who joined through acquisitions.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: Restructuring charge in the quarter, down from $28.5M a year ago.

opex.name: Deferred compensation change
opex.note: Market-related rise in deferred compensation liabilities — pay owed to staff that moves with markets.

otherDetail: Non-operating income of $17.6M: $32.3M of net gains on investments and $3.3M of other gains, partly offset by $18.0M of net losses on consolidated investment products. Total net income was $597.1M; because redeemable noncontrolling interests bore a $15.2M loss, net income attributable to T. Rowe Price Group was $612.3M.
oneTimers: Restructuring charges were $4.0M in the quarter, down from $28.5M a year ago. On the company's adjusted basis — which excludes restructuring, acquisition-related items and similar costs — net income attributable was $629.5M and diluted EPS was $2.86, versus $612.3M and $2.79 on a GAAP basis.
footerNote: T. Rowe Price has no cost-of-revenue line — all of its costs are operating expenses, so gross profit equals revenue in the flow. Net income in the flow is the $612.3M attributable to T. Rowe Price Group, Inc.; total net income was $597.1M before a $15.2M loss allocated to redeemable noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: Fees grew with markets
takeaways.text: Investment advisory fees rose 5.8% to $1,796.4M as average assets under management rose 9.5% to $1,887.2B, partly offset by a lower average fee rate of 37.8 basis points.

takeaways.title: Clients kept pulling money out
takeaways.text: Net client outflows were $28.3B in the quarter, including $25.6B from equity. Ending AUM fell 1.6% in the quarter to $1,862.7B despite the revenue growth.

takeaways.title: Profit dipped on smaller investment gains
takeaways.text: Non-operating income fell to $17.6M from $238.4M a year ago, when investment gains were much larger. Net income for shareholders fell 5.2% to $612.3M, while operating income rose 19.7% to $769.8M.
